newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INTERVIEW-DUTCH AHOLD -- A NATURAL MOTHER.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-DUTCH AHOLD -- A NATURAL MOTHER.

text.p: Dutch supermarket giant Ahold NV receives a dozen approaches a year from companies around the world offering themselves as takeover targets or looking for close ties, chairman Cees van der Hoeven said in an interview on Tuesday.
"(Fifty percent-owned Brazilian supermarket chain) Bompreco approached us...that happens very often.
"Medium-sized and smaller chains lack the bigger chains' economies of scale...It's good for them to have a big brother to lean on if they want to be profitable in the longer-term."
Van der Hoeven said these firms opted for Ahold rather than one of its larger rivals because they were confident the Dutch group would ensure their continuity.

"Continuity is essential to us. In principle, the management, the name, ...remain when we take over. The chain can continue to do most things the way it did before...and gain economies of scale," he said.
Van der Hoeven stressed that Ahold has a policy of not launching hostile bids and other parties were aware of that.
"So a supermarket chain is not scared of us when we show we're interested," he said.
He said Ahold was an attractive parent for many supermarket chains. "A supermarket which wants to keep a relative degree of independence, can find a natural mother in Ahold."
"The major English players are mainly focused on England, (German retail group) Tengelmann mainly expands on an organic basis, Americans don't go out of their country,..."
"We are a rather unique phenomenon in supermarket-land," Van der Hoeven said, adding that this should not be confused with hypermarket chains such as France's Carrefour .
He stressed Ahold was not opportunistic in its takeover strategy, but had clearly defined takeover parameters.

A potential takeover candidate must have sound management for Ahold to take an interest, he said, adding that a chain's culture should also match that of the Dutch group -- being focused on quality and the customer.
Any prospective partner should also have regional market leader potential and good growth or expansion possibilities. Any deal should also, of course, bring financial attractions.
Any deal must at least cover all capital costs and improve earnings per share, preferably from Day One.
"We are currently in the situation where we think we're able to realise that," Van der Hoeven said, referring to immediate earnings per share growth.
Ahold also has minimum demands on balance sheet ratios, targetting 100 percent net gearing on a 25 percent solvency rate in the long-term.
"We can be on the wrong side of this for a while, but in the long-term, we want to stick to these," Van der Hoeven said.
